endorsements.quote: We argue that the utility of the ‘Model Card’ in the hands of its users must be measured through representative quantitative and qualitative assessment, accounting for cultural and international differences.

We advocate for much greater standardization of information supplied to users, with the presentation of this information in highly usable formats, that look the same for every product and use standardized layouts for including, ordering and ranking of information.
The CHAI proposal is a great idea as transparency through a familiar and standardized approach is much needed.

unlisted_practices: Integrate or merge model cards with mandatory medical device labels to avoid duplication of information.
Link model cards to deeper layers of verifiable, open, and regularly refreshed information on model safety and performance.
Independently audit the information presented in model cards and nutrition labels so it is reliable and not deceptive marketing.
Systematically test model cards with users before widespread uptake.
Obtain regulatory acceptance of model cards and nutrition labels.
Provide mechanisms for users to report problems with information in model cards and labels.
Do not use graphical nutrition labels as a substitute for inherently safe design or to convey critical safety information.
Enforce restrictions on direct use of general-purpose AI models by clinicians and patients when model cards and laws state they should not be used that way.

screen.reason: Commentary discussing the use and design of transparent model cards and nutrition labels for health AI and general purpose AI governance.
